{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "packages/core/EventManager.ts",
      "line": 119,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Handle an empty destination list in the Google Meet fallback",
      "body": "When destinationCalendar is null, undefined, or empty, destructuring produces an undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar. Selecting Google Meet then dereferences its integration property and throws instead of falling back to Cal Video as before. This prevents bookings with Google Meet and no destination calendar from completing. Restore the optional access or explicitly handle the missing destination."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/core/EventManager.ts",
      "line": 370,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Select the current host's destination for non-Google adapters",
      "body": "Each host's credential is passed the complete destinationCalendar array, but Office365, Lark, and BaseCalendarService still select only its first element. Consequently, a second host's request uses the first host's calendar ID with the second host's credentials. Office365 and Lark requests fail for unshared calendars; CalDAV filters out every calendar and reports success without creating anything. Scope the destination to the current host or make all adapters resolve it by credentialId."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/core/EventManager.ts",
      "line": 170,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Preserve credentialId on video booking references",
      "body": "The new conditional discards result.credentialId for every non-calendar result, including dedicated video meetings. handleCancelBooking only calls deleteMeeting when the video reference has a credentialId, so newly created Zoom and other video bookings will be cancelled in Cal.com without deleting their underlying meetings. Keep the video result's credentialId when constructing the reference."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts",
      "line": 151,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Retain organization slugs when team billing is disabled",
      "body": "This reverses the original condition for storing slug. With IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED disabled, organization creation now stores neither slug nor metadata.requestedSlug. The organization therefore cannot be resolved through its requested subdomain, and the slug collision query cannot find it on subsequent creation attempts. Preserve the original billing-disabled condition when rewriting this spread."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts",
      "line": 449,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Delete every host's references when cancelling a recurring series",
      "body": "The allRemainingBookings branch ignores the co-host credential fetched by the new outer loop. Instead, it repeatedly iterates the organizer's credentials and selects only the first calendar reference from each occurrence. For a collective recurring series, this deletes the organizer's events repeatedly but never uses the other hosts' credentials or event UIDs. All occurrences are marked cancelled while co-host calendar events remain and continue blocking availability."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/requestReschedule.handler.ts",
      "line": 208,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Use each host reference's credential when requesting a reschedule",
      "body": "Collective bookings now contain calendar references belonging to multiple users, but this deletion path still looks up credentials by integration type from the requesting user's credentials. With two hosts using personal Google accounts, both references are deleted using the requesting host's token; deleting the other host's calendar event fails, and Promise.allSettled hides the failure. The booking is cancelled but the co-host's event remains. Resolve each reference by credentialId, including credentials belonging to the other booked hosts."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts",
      "line": 1078,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Keep co-host destinations when the organizer has no calendar",
      "body": "If neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null. This optional push then does nothing, discarding all connected co-host destinations collected above. A collective event whose first host has no calendar therefore creates no entries for the other hosts, even when their calendars are connected. Initialize an empty array or concatenate the co-host destinations independently of the organizer's destination."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/confirm.handler.ts",
      "line": 175,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Restore collective destinations during deferred confirmation",
      "body": "Only the first destination is persisted on Booking by handleNewBooking. For a collective booking requiring confirmation, this reconstruction therefore supplies EventManager with only the organizer's destination, and approving the booking never creates the co-host calendar entries added by this PR. Rebuild the destination list from the booked collective hosts when confirming; the deferred payment creation paths have the same singleton reconstruction problem."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 147,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Preserve calendar selection for destinations without credentialId",
      "body": "EventManager still supports destinations without a credentialId by selecting credentials according to integration. For those destinations, this lookup cannot match the supplied credential ID, so insertion silently falls back to primary despite a configured destination.externalId. These bookings previously went to the configured calendar and now go to the wrong one. Retain destination selection for this supported credential-less case."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 256,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Use a valid Google calendar fallback when the reference ID is absent",
      "body": "When externalCalendarId is null or omitted, the fallback searches for a destination whose externalId equals that same absent value. Valid destination IDs cannot match, so updates receive an undefined calendarId and fail even when the event has a configured destination. deleteEvent repeats this expression and instead tries primary, potentially leaving non-primary events behind while treating 404 as success. This is reachable through references created without externalId and through CalendarManager.deleteEvent, which omits the argument."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/core/EventManager.ts",
      "line": 495,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "perf",
      "title": "Avoid updating non-traditional calendar references twice",
      "body": "The new filter includes references such as closecom_other_calendar, so the main loop now queues updates for them alongside traditional calendar references. The separate non-traditional integration block below still queues those same updates again. A booking connected to both Google and a CRM therefore sends two concurrent CRM updates for each reschedule, location change, or attendee update, unnecessarily consuming API quota. Exclude other_calendar references from one of these paths."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Handle an empty destination list in the Google Meet fallback
findings.body: When destinationCalendar is null, undefined, or empty, destructuring produces an undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar. Selecting Google Meet then dereferences its integration property and throws instead of falling back to Cal Video as before. This prevents bookings with Google Meet and no destination calendar from completing. Restore the optional access or explicitly handle the missing destination.

findings.title: Select the current host's destination for non-Google adapters
findings.body: Each host's credential is passed the complete destinationCalendar array, but Office365, Lark, and BaseCalendarService still select only its first element. Consequently, a second host's request uses the first host's calendar ID with the second host's credentials. Office365 and Lark requests fail for unshared calendars; CalDAV filters out every calendar and reports success without creating anything. Scope the destination to the current host or make all adapters resolve it by credentialId.

findings.title: Preserve credentialId on video booking references
findings.body: The new conditional discards result.credentialId for every non-calendar result, including dedicated video meetings. handleCancelBooking only calls deleteMeeting when the video reference has a credentialId, so newly created Zoom and other video bookings will be cancelled in Cal.com without deleting their underlying meetings. Keep the video result's credentialId when constructing the reference.

findings.title: Retain organization slugs when team billing is disabled
findings.body: This reverses the original condition for storing slug. With IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED disabled, organization creation now stores neither slug nor metadata.requestedSlug. The organization therefore cannot be resolved through its requested subdomain, and the slug collision query cannot find it on subsequent creation attempts. Preserve the original billing-disabled condition when rewriting this spread.

findings.title: Delete every host's references when cancelling a recurring series
findings.body: The allRemainingBookings branch ignores the co-host credential fetched by the new outer loop. Instead, it repeatedly iterates the organizer's credentials and selects only the first calendar reference from each occurrence. For a collective recurring series, this deletes the organizer's events repeatedly but never uses the other hosts' credentials or event UIDs. All occurrences are marked cancelled while co-host calendar events remain and continue blocking availability.

findings.title: Use each host reference's credential when requesting a reschedule
findings.body: Collective bookings now contain calendar references belonging to multiple users, but this deletion path still looks up credentials by integration type from the requesting user's credentials. With two hosts using personal Google accounts, both references are deleted using the requesting host's token; deleting the other host's calendar event fails, and Promise.allSettled hides the failure. The booking is cancelled but the co-host's event remains. Resolve each reference by credentialId, including credentials belonging to the other booked hosts.

findings.title: Keep co-host destinations when the organizer has no calendar
findings.body: If neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null. This optional push then does nothing, discarding all connected co-host destinations collected above. A collective event whose first host has no calendar therefore creates no entries for the other hosts, even when their calendars are connected. Initialize an empty array or concatenate the co-host destinations independently of the organizer's destination.

findings.title: Restore collective destinations during deferred confirmation
findings.body: Only the first destination is persisted on Booking by handleNewBooking. For a collective booking requiring confirmation, this reconstruction therefore supplies EventManager with only the organizer's destination, and approving the booking never creates the co-host calendar entries added by this PR. Rebuild the destination list from the booked collective hosts when confirming; the deferred payment creation paths have the same singleton reconstruction problem.

findings.title: Preserve calendar selection for destinations without credentialId
findings.body: EventManager still supports destinations without a credentialId by selecting credentials according to integration. For those destinations, this lookup cannot match the supplied credential ID, so insertion silently falls back to primary despite a configured destination.externalId. These bookings previously went to the configured calendar and now go to the wrong one. Retain destination selection for this supported credential-less case.

findings.title: Use a valid Google calendar fallback when the reference ID is absent
findings.body: When externalCalendarId is null or omitted, the fallback searches for a destination whose externalId equals that same absent value. Valid destination IDs cannot match, so updates receive an undefined calendarId and fail even when the event has a configured destination. deleteEvent repeats this expression and instead tries primary, potentially leaving non-primary events behind while treating 404 as success. This is reachable through references created without externalId and through CalendarManager.deleteEvent, which omits the argument.

findings.title: Avoid updating non-traditional calendar references twice
findings.body: The new filter includes references such as closecom_other_calendar, so the main loop now queues updates for them alongside traditional calendar references. The separate non-traditional integration block below still queues those same updates again. A booking connected to both Google and a CRM therefore sends two concurrent CRM updates for each reschedule, location change, or attendee update, unnecessarily consuming API quota. Exclude other_calendar references from one of these paths.
